text:
marta: Hey team, CI deploys started failing on the model-artifacts upload step for a couple of customers — job 4552. Last night we tightened service-account permissions and I think something got too strict. Error from the pipeline: 

```
Uploading artifacts...
10.0.0.3 - 403 Forbidden
Error: Permission denied when requesting token to impersonate service account: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied
Failed to sign upload URL: 403
```

marta: This only started ~2 hours after the permissions change. Link to pipeline: https://ci.redwood.dev/runs/4552 

devon: ugh. can you paste the service account that's being impersonated by the runner? also which runner identity is doing the impersonation (i.e. the principal that needs the Token Creator role)? :eyes:

marta: The pipeline is set to impersonate `redwood-ci-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (target SA). The runner principal (the identity of the CI worker) is `github-actions[org:redwood,repo:infra]` via our OIDC provider (we call it ci-runner@redwood-svc). We recently removed a broad role from **ci-runner**.

devon: ok likely the runner lost `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the target SA. Quick repro: from a shell where you can call the CI identity (or locally via your user), you can try impersonation to see the exact error:

```bash
# try to get a short-lived token for the target SA
gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=redwood-ci-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# or using the OIDC token exchange path we use in CI:
curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"audience":"https://token.redwood.dev","subject_token_type":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt","requested_token_type":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token","subject_token":"<OIDC_JWT>"}' \
  https://sts.example.com/token | jq .
```

devon: If the impersonation fails you'll see the same 403 + text saying principal is missing roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator.

samir: Confirming — I hit this earlier with a different tenant. The fix is to give the CI principal the Token Creator role on the *target* service account, not Editor/Owner. For GCP that is `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`. Example check: 

```bash
# inspect bindings on target SA
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy redwood-ci-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json | jq .bindings
```

samir: If missing, add it (temporary quick fix):

```bash
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding \
  redwood-ci-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-svc.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
```

marta: ran that as a test, and the upload step moved past the token error. deploys succeeded after the binding was added :tada:

marta: But we shouldn't leave it that way — previously ci-runner had a broad role on the project which we removed intentionally. We need least-privilege: token-creator only on the target SA and with conditions if possible. Also we should avoid long-lived keys on the target SA.

devon: Agreed. Action plan:
- Add Token Creator binding scoped to only the target SA for the CI principal (done as temporary).
- Create infra PR to manage this via Terraform (no manual state drift).
- Add a condition on the binding to restrict impersonation to the CI repo/branch or to the OIDC aud claim if provider supports it.
- Add CI test that attempts impersonation during PR validation so this breaks in CI preview not prod.

ops-oncall: bumping to ops for review, logging incident and assigning a tracking ticket: #INC-2107. Please include the evidence lines (the `get-iam-policy` output you pasted) and the test that validated the fix.

ci-bot: Deploy job 4552 resumed after permission binding change by marta (log: https://ci.redwood.dev/runs/4552/logs) :white_check_mark:

samir: For the infra PR, use a terraform snippet like this (we scope it to the SA resource):

```hcl
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ci_token_creator" {
  service_account_id = "redwood-ci-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  role               = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
  members            = ["serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-svc.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
  # optional: add condition to limit aud/actor
}
```
samir: Also consider switching the pipeline to a short TTL (we already support 30s-5m impersonated tokens). That reduces blast radius.

marta: Opening PR now: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/merge_requests/142 — includes the binding + a short CI job that uses the impersonation path to validate. Leaving the temporary manual binding up until the MR lands and CI validates.

devon: Thanks. Follow-ups: add a note in the runbook under `support/ci/impersonation` describing how to debug (gcloud command, log paths, error strings to look for), and add an alert if CI fails with the specific 403 token error for >3 consecutive runs.

ops-oncall: assigned to @samir for the PR review and to @marta for verification after merge. Closing this incident once infra MR is merged and the manual binding is removed. :lock:

marta: thanks all — will update INC-2107 when the MR is merged and confirm we rotated any long-lived keys we found.
